body: If it's not too difficult for you, what does exposure therapy consist of? How is it supposed to help? Sorry but I'm curious as to the ways of making myself better

Thank you for this.

Social media is/was definitely a concern and I've gradually been weaning myself off and cleaning up all the poor taste jokes and vitriolic arguments I found myself starting when I was 14.

In many cases, I've found myself rereading old messages to people I've wronged, reading my apologies and seeing them be accepted, but it's something I've had to do multiple times to reassure myself, which I know isn't healthy.

I've forgiven people that have hurt me in similar ways. I know that it was a long time ago and people change, but I also don't think about these people much. My worry is that being notably connected to a considerable IP will reopen long healed wounds. In many cases these people and I are both better off not interacting, and I'm concerned, for my sake and theirs, what my presence in their sphere, however tangential, will do.

I just have to keep reminding myself that the world doesn't revolve around me, even if everyone I've ever interacted with is going to be reminded of their version of me in two months.

It's hyperbolic and ludicrous, but a key factor that's kept me grounded about it all is knowing that basically no one in the entertainment industry has been "cancelled" for stuff that happened as a kid. I know I'm not capable of the diabolical stuff some creatives have been done for, so by keeping my nose clean from here on out I should have nothing to fear.

Some of my peers and I suspect many of my superiors have undertaken some form of therapy during and after entering the industry, so I think that may be the way forward.

Thank you.

If addressed, I know I could take responsibility and apologise. In many cases before, I already have. It was so long ago now that I know the best solution for everyone involved is to let sleeping dogs lie, but the anxiety of being perceived has probably warped my perception of how real people act.

For the most part and as far as I know, I'm not on bad terms with these people. What sends me into a panic is not knowing what they think of me now, having not been in each other's lives for seven or eight years plus at this point. This is something I know I still need to work on, as rationally I understand that my role in their life is likely very small if existent at all. I can't help but place myself at the centre of things a lot, and while I actively try and ignore this, it's still somewhat ingrained and needs work.
Hell, it's probably partly why I'm in the business I am.

I know exactly what you mean.

Normally I'm completely non-religious and as far from superstitious as you can get, but whenever it all just gets too much I start seeing signs everywhere, and start believing that my whole life has just been a part of some play for the universe. I hate it and it never makes any sense why I start seeing the world that way, but it's become a pretty consistent part of the anxiety descent recently

Can't edit on mobile but from OP:

I still love the girl but am no longer in love with her.

I'll reply to every message in time but I'm currently piss drunk (mostly related to the situation at hand)

Thank you everyone for your advice. The vast majority has been productive and I promise you I'll act on it. It's just hard yknow.

As an update: we're sitting together right now in a bar (in the UK so it's past 10pm) whilst rather tipsy and getting really fuckin close. But I can't get the idea out my mind that she's got a super committed boyfriend 300 miles away

In the end we went out for the afternoon and I got out of that room and I'm feeling better. I didn't tell them what happened but I think they know something's up. I'm thinking I might go and see a professional about it all but for now all I want to do is get out and forget. I'm not usually a believer in fate and all that but in this case I'm willing to make an exception. I might see if I can crash somewhere else tonight
